4. As per the prosecution story, the informant's minor daughter went to a shop to purchase household items on 26.01.2021 at around 04:00 P.M. However, she did not return home that evening, thereafter, the informant along with the other relatives and villagers started searching for her.
During their inquiry, they came to know that the victim was last seen with the appellant and the co-accused Arjun Mahto.
Thereafter, they went to the appellant's house to enquire about the whereabouts of the victim, but instead of providing any information, the accused persons assaulted them.
It is further alleged that the accused persons kidnapped her daughter.

5. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that in this case from the written information (Exhibit-P/1) it would Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.502 of 2025(4) dt.29-01-2026 appear that the informant has stated the age of the victim as 17 years and she has stated that the victim had left her house in the evening of 26.01.2021 to purchase some articles from the shop, but thereafter she had not returned home.
The written information had been submitted to the police station at Ujiyarpur only on 16.02.2021, i.e. after 21 days of the occurrence.

6. Learned counsel further submits that in her statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C., the victim has clearly stated that she was not allured or kidnapped by anyone rather she was in an affair outside her marriage with the appellant and on her own volition she had left her house and went with the appellant to marry with him.
She has further stated that she had married with the appellant in Morwa Temple and thereafter, they were living at Muzaffarpur in a rented house.
She has accepted her marriage on her own will and volition.

7. Learned counsel further submits that to prove the age of the victim, the prosecution introduced one Sanjay Kumar Sinha (P.W.3), who had deposed with the Admission Register of the School at the instance of the District Education Officer.

He has stated that he is the Principal of the said school and in the Register at Serial No.79 for the Academic Session 2012-13, the Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.502 of 2025(4) dt.29-01-2026 name of the victim is mentioned with her date of birth as '15.05.2004', but he has clearly stated that there is no mention that on what basis the admission of the victim had been done.
In the Admission Register, the entries have been made in the pen of the former Principal Bela Kumari, but she has already died.

It is thus submitted that the basis of the entries made in the Admission Register has not been proved by the prosecution, further the medical examination report disclosed the age of the victim between 17 and half 18 years.
8. The appellant in this case was 29 years old, both of them have married and have got two children out of the said marriage.

9. Learned counsel for the informant has not opposed the prayer of the appellant for suspension of his sentence and release on bail, as according to him, the victim is already living with the appellant and the children.

sentences.text:
Having regard to the entire facts and circumstances, particularly as recorded in Paragraph '8'
above we direct suspension of sentence and release on bail of the appellant during pendency of the appeal.

Let the sentence of the appellant be suspended and he be released on bail, during pendency of the appeal, on furnishing bail bond of Rs.25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand Only) with two Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.502 of 2025(4) dt.29-01-2026 sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Exclusive Special Judge (Rape and POCSO), Samastipur in T.R. No. 05 of 2021, Reg. No. 827/2022 arising out of Ujiyarpur P.S. Case No. 38 of 2021.
11.
The fine, if any, imposed as a part of sentence shall remain suspended during pendency of the appeal.

12. It is clarified that the observations made hereinabove are only prima-facie and tentative in nature for purpose of consideration of prayer for suspension of sentence and bail of the appellant which would not cause prejudice to either of the parties.

13. List this appeal for hearing on its turn.
(Rajeev Ranjan Prasad, J) ( Praveen Kumar, J) shivam/-
